opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jennifer Martin (E033), full-time Analyst, requests admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee she can have up to write, and admin only if her role owns the system. Analyst does not own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does), so the maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jennifer Martin (E033) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so maximum is read. Recommend read.
reason: Jennifer Martin (E033) requested admin access to Payroll. The two notes conflict on employment status: HR lists her as a full-time Analyst (max write; admin only if her role owns the system — Analyst does not own Payroll), while Security lists her as a contractor with basic security training (max read; never admin). Applying the more restrictive maximum, she is entitled to at most read. The requested admin level exceeds the maximum, so grant read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Jennifer Martin (E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory has two notes:
- Note 1: HR says role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation for Payroll: write. Comment says full-time Analyst, can have up to write, admin only if role owns system. Analyst does not own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does), so maximum is write. Recommend write.
- Note 2: Security says contractor, basic security training. Recommendation: read. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Maximum is read.

There's a conflict between HR (full_time) and Security (contractor). The two notes disagree on employment type. Hmm.

Which to trust? As the Approver, I need to make a decision. The notes conflict on employment status. Given conflicting information, I should probably consider the more restrictive/secure option, or consider which source is authoritative for employment type. HR typically owns employment type. Security DB shows contractor status.

Actually, let's think. The HR agent wrote employment type full_time; the Security agent wrote contractor. There is a conflict. The policy: full_time up to write, admin only if role owns system (Analyst doesn't own Payroll, so max write). Contractor: read, or write with advanced training; basic training, so max read.

Given conflicting info, security-conscious approach would be to grant the lower of the two maximums: read. The Security agent recommends read; HR recommends write. Since we cannot verify which is correct, conservative decision would be read.

But which information should the Approver rely on? The team memory says "Employee facts written on an earlier ticket are shown on later tickets." Here both notes are on ticket 1, same ticket. There's a discrepancy.

I think the safe decision is to grant the maximum based on the more restrictive interpretation: read. Requested admin is above read, so grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Reason: Jennifer Martin requested admin for Payroll. Notes conflict: HR lists full-time Analyst (max write, not admin since Analyst doesn't own Payroll), Security lists contractor with basic training (max read, never admin). Given conflicting records, apply the more restrictive maximum of read. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so grant read.
